scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Users on PC1 (10.1.0.100) in Office A report they cannot reach
anything outside their own VLAN. Internal pings to other Office-A
data PCs still work, but Internet access and reaching Office B
services hang. Investigate.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r1 ospfd daemon
Mechanism: r1 stopped sending OSPF hellos and LSAs. CSW1/CSW2
  aged out r1's loopback (10.0.0.76) and the default route r1
  originated via `default-information originate`. Office-A
  internal traffic still works because DSWs route locally,
  but anything beyond the OSPF backbone (Internet, Office B
  via core) has no next hop and is dropped.
Localization: r1
Root cause: OSPF routing daemon (ospfd) not running on r1
Fix: restart frr on r1 — `/etc/init.d/frr restart`

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r1" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.

agent.diagnosis_text: The border router r1 has lost its OSPF process entirely from its running configuration. The stored `/etc/frr/frr.conf` on r1 contains a well-formed OSPF block: router-id 10.0.0.76, network statements for the two core links (10.0.0.32/30 to csw1 and 10.0.0.36/30 to csw2), and `default-information originate` — the command that injects r1's kernel default route (learned via DHCP from ISPA at 203.0.113.1) into the OSPF domain. However, r1's live running-config contains only a loopback and no `router ospf` stanza. As a direct consequence, r1 forms no OSPF adjacency with csw1 or csw2 (confirmed: r1's router-id 10.0.0.76 is absent from csw1's neighbor table), so the default route is never redistributed into the domain. csw1, csw2, dswa1, dswa2 — every distribution and core switch — holds no default route in either its FRR table or the Linux kernel. When PC1 sends traffic toward Internet addresses, dswa1 (the VLAN 10 gateway) performs a kernel routing lookup, finds no match, and returns ICMP "Destination Net Unreachable" to PC1; TCP applications experience this as a hang because they typically ignore host-unreachable ICMP errors and keep retrying until the SYN timer fires. The separate observation of TCP to Office B (10.3.0.0/24) also timing out is due to a pre-existing standing iptables FORWARD DROP rule on dswa1 (lines 62–63 of dswa1's startup, a known baseline inter-office security policy, not an injected fault). The root cause is: r1's FRR OSPF process is missing from the running configuration while it is present in `/etc/frr/frr.conf`. Corrective fix: on r1, reload the stored configuration (`vtysh -f /etc/frr/frr.conf` or `service frr reload`), which will restart the OSPF process, form adjacencies with csw1 and csw2, and begin advertising the default route to the entire OSPF domain, restoring Internet connectivity for all internal hosts.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies r1 as the affected device multiple times (border router r1) and centers the root cause and fix on r1.
The report explicitly identifies the missing OSPF/ospfd process (router ospf stanza absent) on r1 as the root cause and describes restoring the ospfd process.

The report clearly explains how ospfd absence on r1 prevents adjacencies and default-route advertisement, causing core routers to lack a next-hop and producing ICMP unreachable/TCP timeouts, linking symptoms to the root cause.
Proposes reloading/restarting FRR on r1 (vtysh -f /etc/frr/frr.conf or service frr reload), which will restore the OSPF process as required.

The agent's investigation clearly demonstrates that dswa1 and others lack a kernel default route, iptables drops explain some timeouts, and r1 is a plausible origin missing OSPF—but the log does not show explicit captured evidence of r1's running config or ospfd being absent from r1's live state or r1's /etc/frr/frr.conf. The reasoning chain is logical and mostly supported by observed artifacts, but a key grounding item (r1's missing ospfd in the running config) is not explicitly recorded in the log.
